items.title: Adapt Pulse into the 3F app base
items.story: Vendor Pulse into the repo, reskin to KnackLabs green, run on Postgres, keep OTP auth — so the app boots on our stack.
acceptance_criteria: App builds and boots on the npm workspace (backend/frontend/contract)
Login works (email+OTP) and the shell renders in KnackLabs green, branded 3F
A Postgres warehouse adapter runs a trivial query end-to-end
3oilpalm harness machinery intact (dual-runtime + vendor integrity clean)
items.outcome: The 3F platform base is shipped end-to-end (all 10 platform-base tasks merged to master, CI green): a vendored NestJS backend on a separate Postgres warehouse with cookie-based email/OTP auth, a trimmed loopback-hardened API allow-list, app-wide observability (a governed constitution-07 error envelope + structured JSON request/error logging correlated by correlationId), a Next.js App Router frontend shell + two-step email/OTP login faithful to the imported 3F design and _ds tokens, and a repo-wide quality gate across all three workspaces (contract+backend+frontend) with dual-runtime + vendor-integrity checks and CI verify on every push. A user can sign in to the shell; the factory can build, verify, and ship the next epic on a green, guarded foundation.

items.title: Ingest SAP actuals + budgets
items.story: Ingest the SAP Base Report (Excel) and the plan budgets into Postgres at monthly grain, retaining raw lines.
acceptance_criteria: July SAP load reconciles to report totals (nursery net ~ Rs 1,15,12,712)
Budgets ingested from the MIS format as a separate object
Raw transaction lines retained for drill-down
Re-uploading a month replaces it idempotently (no duplicates)
items.outcome: sap-ingestion delivers the Financial MIS data foundation: SAP actuals and MIS budgets ingest into a dedicated warehouse (guarded POST /api/ingest/actuals and /budget), each upload replaced idempotently per period with prior-batch retention, and the headline figure is proven to source — July 2026 DUB actuals reconcile to EXACTLY Rs 11,512,712.07 (paise) across both the raw sap_transaction rows and the actual_by_key_month gold view, stable under re-upload. Four tasks shipped: warehouse-schema (#13), actuals-loader (#15), budget-loader (#16), reconciliation-proof (#17). No governed budget-actual join or UI yet (governed-joins / reporting stories).

items.title: Financial semantic layer + governed joins
items.story: Define Actual/Budget/Rollover/% measures in code and compose Budget-Actual with a validated full-outer join.
acceptance_criteria: % = Actual / Budget computes correctly across the two objects, incl. zero-filled rows
Governed-join golden fixture passes; no fan-out / double-counting
RBAC row-scope injected on both objects
items.outcome: The 3F MIS now has ONE governed financial definition — Actual, Budget and % — that report, drill-down and the assistant all share, computed over a correct Budget-Actual join instead of ad-hoc SQL. Each source is first reduced to one ACTIVE row per (gl_code, month), so Budget no longer fans out across a GL's Actual cost centres; the two are then FULL-OUTER-joined with zero-fill, so a Budget-only or Actual-only GL still appears (valued 0.00) instead of vanishing. The % follows the confirmed nil rule in one place: blank/NA when both sides are zero, 'over-budget' when actual spend exists against no budget, and 'credit / negative actual' when that actual is a credit. Access is fail-closed at the single execution boundary — a governed-financial read action plus the domain and every selected measure and dimension grant — and row scope is applied to BOTH sources, so a user scoped away from DUB sees no DUB Budget rows. Every governed number is now explainable: the same composed query returns which sides fed each row (matched / budget-only / actual-only), the deterministic Budget-Components label set, and the ACTIVE source batch ids as (source, period, batch) tuples, with one-sided rows citing only the batch that actually contributed — so when a reload changes an answer, it is attributable to that batch swap. Correctness is frozen behind a golden-answer fixture asserting exact values for all six cases (matched, Budget-only, Actual-only, duplicate/no-fan-out, reload/active-swap, %-edges), demonstrated against a real warehouse (13/13, with a dead-port control proving the proof genuinely connects). This unblocks the MIS reporting epic: the statement, its drill-down and the assistant can now select governed measures rather than author SQL.

items.title: Selection + mapping master
items.story: Department/Function/Plant selection resolved via a provisional mapping master; composite-key validation.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting Agriculture/Nursery/DUB returns exactly the DUB nursery slice
Output does not depend on the source file name
A selection with no mapping renders zeros + a 'no mapping configured' notice
items.outcome: mis-selection ships the selection layer end to end. A versioned repo-owned Mapping Master is now the single authority for plant aliases, the MIS format and the (cost centre, GL) to MIS-line mapping, with the nine unresolved DUB triples held in an explicit unmapped-GL bucket rather than inferred or dropped. Selection narrows the governed path rather than forking it - the master's resolved triples filter the Actual side before the (gl_code, month) roll-up - and two governed routes expose it. An authenticated user opens MIS Reports, picks Agriculture / Nursery / DUB and a period, presses Generate, and sees the DUB nursery slice from real SAP data: the resolved scope, the totals, the governed GL rows, and the unmapped-GL bucket as a reviewable list carrying an Actual and a Budget amount per GL with the reason each one is unmapped. That list is the artifact that goes to Srihari to get the authoritative mapping back.

items.title: MIS statement + Excel export
items.story: Render the exact grouped Budget/Actual/% statement (July + FY-YTD) with a clean structured Excel export.
acceptance_criteria: Nursery July statement reconciles to SAP-derived totals
Zero-rows present; subtotals and grand total foot correctly
Excel export opens with the same structure
items.outcome: 3F can produce the Financial MIS themselves. Pick Agriculture / Nursery / DUB and a period, and Srihari's own statement appears - his hierarchy at its natural depth, his line numbers and budget components, the month and the year-to-date side by side, every parent footing to a grand total of Rs 1,15,12,712 Actual against Rs 1,00,50,136 Budget for July. Download Excel hands him the same statement as a real spreadsheet whose columns sum, named for the selection it came from. The unmapped-GL line stays visible throughout, so the mapping gap he still owes us is impossible to miss rather than absorbed into a total.

items.title: Actuals drill-down to transactions
items.story: 2-level drill (group to sub-lines to transactions), Actuals-only, RBAC-scoped and audited.
acceptance_criteria: Line-item footer total equals the clicked Actual
Default sort Value largest-to-lowest then Month latest-to-oldest; Budget/% not clickable
User sees only transactions within their RBAC scope; each drill is audited
items.outcome: Finance can now click any Actual on the Financial MIS and see how it was built. Clicking a group - or the Grand Total - opens a flattened list of every descendant leaf beneath it, footing to the clicked figure in exact paise; clicking a leaf, including the unmapped-GL line, opens the SAP transaction lines behind it in seven columns with a footer that matches the number on the statement. The drill is pinned to the exact actuals and budget batches the displayed statement was built from, so a re-upload can never silently change the answer under the reader's finger: a replaced batch is read and named, and a pin that no longer covers the range is refused with instructions to generate the statement again. Every drill writes a typed audit record before a single row is read and fails closed if that write fails, and refused attempts are audited too - this is the system's only raw-row read path, the documented exception to the aggregate-only rules, so it is the one place where who read which transactions is recoverable. Proven against the client's July extract: a leaf and the unmapped bucket foot in exact paise, the Grand Total reaches 1,00,50,136.29 Budget and 1,15,12,712.07 Actual, and opening a group issues no network request at all.

items.title: Assistant + exploration
items.story: Natural-language assistant + saved reports/dashboards over the governed layer; conversational but read-only on numbers.
acceptance_criteria: An NL data question returns a verified, provenanced answer matching the report; no fabricated numbers
General chat handled naturally; off-topic questions nudged back to the report
A saved report re-runs correctly under the user's RBAC
items.outcome: Srihari can now ask the 3F Financial MIS questions in plain English and get answers he can check. The assistant is registered and governed: every question runs through the same authorization, semantic layer and SQL guard as the reports, so an answer is either the governed numbers with a verified badge and its provenance - the readback, the measures, the scope and the data-as-of behind a disclosure - or an honest refusal that says why. It declines what it must not answer: a causal 'why is labour high' is refused rather than guessed at, a question outside the registered catalog returns not-supported rather than a plausible number, and a greeting is answered deterministically without ever reaching the model. Answers are asked and read in two places, the panel docked beside the MIS report and a standalone Ask page, and 'view in report' opens the statement the answer came from, or says plainly why it cannot. He can save a question and pin it to his dashboard, then reopen either from Explore or the dashboard - and reopening RE-RUNS the saved selection against current data rather than replaying a stored answer, because nothing at rest holds one: the vendored snapshot machinery was deleted outright. Every reopen re-authorizes as the current user against the current semantic layer, so a selection he may no longer run comes back as a refusal that says so rather than a stale figure or a silently missing row, and it stays visible and deletable. The model runs on Bedrock in ap-south-1, and the boundary is enforced by test on the provider's own arguments: his question, the prior turns and the governed vocabulary may leave the app; amounts, measure values, transaction lines and result rows never do.

items.title: Assistant responsiveness and shell truth
items.story: As Srihari, I want the assistant to show me it is working and the shell to tell me the truth about the data, so that a 40-second answer does not look like a hang and a dead 'Freshness unavailable' chip does not make the product look broken.
acceptance_criteria: Both Ask surfaces stream the backend's existing routing/selecting/querying/summarizing phases instead of showing a bare spinner
A model response that never emits a tool block is retried once under a bounded output cap, rather than silently returning noToolUse or running unbounded
The shell's freshness pill shows the real warehouse data-as-of, and the docked Ask panel fills its column
items.outcome: A follow-up question used to take 39 seconds, then 57, and looked like the product had hung. It now comes back in one to five seconds, and while it works you can see it working: both Ask surfaces stream the backend's own progress phases - routing, selecting, querying, summarizing - instead of one silent spinner, and an answer that arrives immediately shows no flicker at all. The cause turned out to be a single missing request field: the selector call to Bedrock set no output limit, so on a follow-up the model would emit up to twenty-four thousand tokens of preamble around a hundred-token answer. Capping it ended the runaway without truncating anything. Leaving the assistant now actually stops the work rather than abandoning it, and asking a ninth question in one conversation no longer fails - the client sends only as much history as the server accepts. The shell's top bar stops lying: where it showed a permanently greyed-out 'Freshness unavailable' chip, it now shows when the governed data was last loaded, taken from the oldest active batch across actuals and budget so it never claims the numbers are fresher than the stalest input behind them, and it says plainly which kind of unavailable it is when there is nothing to show. The docked Ask panel fills its column instead of stopping halfway down the page.

items.title: Recoverable periods in Ask
items.story: As someone asking a statement question, I want the assistant to ask me which period it should use instead of refusing, and to let me move any answer to another period, so that a missing word costs me a click rather than a retype.
acceptance_criteria: A statement question whose period is missing, not offered, or spans more than one period returns ClarificationNeeded naming the missing part, never NotSupported.
Offered options contain only periods that can answer that question, and never one that is guaranteed to fail, such as a multi-month range for a statement.
Choosing an offered period issues exactly zero selector calls, proven by a hermetic test that counts calls on a fake provider: one for the original question, none for the continuation.
An unresolvable or ambiguous scope triple returns a message naming the attribute and directing the user to an administrator, offers no period options, and is reported ahead of period.
No mapping configured and no periods loaded each keep their own distinct outcome and message, and neither is reported as a missing period.

A successful data answer in either domain displays the period or window it ran on and offers the other periods that could answer it; choosing one replaces that answer in place and the replacement displays the new period.
A successful answer that resolved to no window states that it covers all loaded data and offers no defaulted period control; informational, clarification and failure responses offer none.
A re-run's provenance reports the active batch ids that produced the displayed values, and the determinism claim is about selector calls, not about values being stable across reloads.
Every criterion is proven by hermetic tests over a fake provider and warehouse; any claim made against the live PoC names its sample count and no live claim rests on a single run.
items.outcome: A statement question that names no period now asks which period to use instead of refusing, and every settled answer carries a control that moves it to another period without retyping the question. Measured before: 'Show the MIS statement Actual by statement leaf' returned a red refusal 4/4. Measured after: it returns the prompt and the loaded periods, and clicking one returns 81 verified rows with zero selector calls - the chosen period reaches the warehouse as data, never as words re-guessed by the model. Four failure causes that shared one dead-end message now resolve in a fixed order, each saying what is actually wrong: an unresolvable scope triple points at an administrator, a missing mapping and an empty period list keep their own messages, and only a missing period clarifies. An answer that covers no single period says so - 'All loaded data within your access scope and any filters applied by this question' - rather than defaulting a control to a period it never used.

items.title: All plants in the MIS statement
items.story: As Srihari, I want to pick any of 3F's plants and get its Financial MIS on the same format, with a dash where no budget has been loaded, so that the report covers the whole company and not only the nursery.
acceptance_criteria: Every SAP plant code in the July actuals batch (31) is offered to a fully granted user, each renders a statement, and the 31 Grand Total Actuals sum to the batch's company-wide net of ₹11,02,73,718.00 in exact paise, proven by a warehouse fixture.

The DUB nursery statement is unchanged: Actual ₹1,15,12,712.07 and Budget ₹1,00,50,136.29 for July 2026, parents footing to leaves, the unmapped-GL line carrying its own Actual, and the Excel export matching.

Every (plant, cost centre, GL) triple in the July extract resolves exactly once via a master generated from the full mapping sheet (decision 0031), nothing dropped or fanned out, the eleven unnamed pairs bucketed with a reason, every new master row flagged provisional, and the format naming DUB as its budget owner.

A plant other than the budget owner carries a not-loaded budget state (decision 0033) and renders a dash with the label 'Budget not loaded for this plant' in Budget, Roll-over and % on every row including Grand Total, on screen and in Excel, with no over-budget or credit flag; H.O shows 100% of its net inside Manpower and Admin.
Department and Function labels follow the classification rule (nursery plants Agriculture / Nursery, H.O Corporate / Office, others Operations / Unit), stored and displayed as provisional.
Drill-down foots in exact paise for a leaf and the unmapped-GL line of a non-owner plant with the shipped pin contract; Budget and % stay inert.
The assistant is untouched: its hermetic suite passes unchanged; a user granted only DUB sees only DUB in MIS Reports options and drill-down with no row leaking (decision 0036).

The demo user is granted every canonical plant; the two zero states and three nil states stay distinct from the not-loaded state, all proven by hermetic tests judged by junit testcase name and executed count.

Plant-keyed budget batches, the outline object, the plant upload field, the partial-FY-YTD rule, cascading selection tuples, upload plant reporting, the master-version pin and the plant-aware assistant are deferred together with decision 0033's trigger and are not part of this story.
items.outcome: Every one of the 31 SAP plants in the July extract is now selectable on the MIS Reports screen and renders its own statement on the nursery format, where before only DUB could be chosen. The Department, Function and Plant selectors depend on each other: picking a plant fills in its department and function, picking a department leaves only its functions and plants, and a choice that no longer fits is cleared. The mapping master is generated by a committed script from the client's SAP mapping sheet plus a plant classification table (version 3, 31 plants, 454 cost-centre/GL triples), so a new sheet is a regeneration, not a hand edit; plants whose labels are inferred are marked 'Provisional labels'. Measured: the 31 rendered statements sum to the company net of ₹11,02,73,718.00 in exact paise, and DUB is unchanged against the frozen shipped baseline in values, tree, provenance and Excel bytes. Budget exists only for DUB in the PoC, so every other plant shows a dash for Budget, Roll-over and % (never a zero, never a percentage against nothing) on screen, in the drill and in the export, with an accessible label saying the budget is not loaded for that plant. A user's plant grants come from the seed list, so a demo user can be scoped to one plant. The assistant is untouched by this story.

items.title: Reopening a saved report returns to its answer
items.story: As someone with pinned reports, I want opening one to take me straight to its answer and refresh it in place, so that I get current numbers without a thread full of duplicates.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a saved report whose resolved Selection already has a successful turn re-runs that turn and appends nothing; the thread length is unchanged.
Turn identity is the Selection, never the displayed title: two reports sharing a selectionLabel title but differing in dimensions or filters produce two distinct turns.
When several successful turns carry the same selection, the most recent is the one re-run.
A matched turn re-runs with turn.question and the request body is asserted, not inferred; a new turn uses the label.
Opening a report that is not in the thread appends exactly one turn.
Clicking Open navigates to Ask before the request completes, and the target turn is scrolled into view and shown pending.
A reopen refused for authorization or policy clears the stale result and shows the reason; a transport failure keeps the previous answer; neither shows period-specific copy.
Pins and saved views are both covered by the leaves.
Every criterion is proven by hermetic tests judged by the vitest discriminator - present AND NOT skipped AND NOT failed.
items.outcome: Opening a saved report or pinned report now returns you to its existing answer instead of stacking a duplicate copy of it. The Ask panel opens immediately on the click rather than after the answer arrives, the target turn is scrolled into view and shows 'Opening this report...' while it runs, and the answer it re-runs is re-asked in your own original wording rather than the pin's measure-name label - so the audit record carries the question someone actually asked. Which turn a report belongs to is decided by strict structural comparison of the resolved selection, not the displayed title, so two pins that both read 'Actual - Budget' but cover different dimensions or periods stay separate answers. A reopen refused because access was withdrawn clears the stale numbers from the screen and says why, while the period control's shipped behaviour of keeping the previous answer is untouched - the caller now states which it wants.

items.title: The on-screen assistant explains a number on the MIS statement
items.story: As a finance user looking at a figure on the MIS statement, I want to click it and ask the assistant how it was built, so that I can see which GL codes and cost centres feed that line and which transactions add up to it without leaving the report or guessing.
acceptance_criteria: The docked MIS assistant sends statementGrounding - department, function, plant, period, block, pinned batches and the clicked node - and /ask sends none of it and is byte-for-byte unchanged, proven by its shipped leaves passing unmodified.

The server re-derives every input: department and function from the master's selection for that plant, the plant against the user's current grants, and the pins validated before any read. A tampered nodeKey, block or pin set is refused, not answered.

Intent is a closed enum - composition, causal, data - with stated precedence; a composition question is answered with the explanation, a causal question is still declined with today's copy, and a data question is answered by the existing ungrounded path with no pin or budget promise attached.

A leaf answer names the roll-up path and lists transactions with an exact footer asserted in paise against the statement payload, the true total count, the first 20 rows inline, and a control that opens the shipped drill panel for the rest.
A total or subtotal answer names the lines that compose it and their GLs and cost centres with no raw rows and no warehouse query, so decision 0024 holds and no governed-read audit is implied.

No transaction row, amount, batch identifier or result row ever reaches the model - a leaf asserts the provider payload, not the rendered answer - and the leaf read carries the drill's governed-read protections with the predicate audited before the query and failing closed.

Staleness follows decision 0025: a replaced-but-present batch is read and reported, only a gone batch is refused, and both are typed with source, period and batch status rather than flattened by the global error envelope.
items.outcome: Click any Actual figure on the MIS statement, ask the assistant beside it how that number came to be, and get an answer built from the same governed data the figure came from. A leaf line answers with both halves: the roll-up path naming the GL codes and cost centres the mapping master folds into it, and the transactions behind it with a footer that foots in paise to the cell you clicked. A subtotal or grand total answers with the lines that compose it and their values, projected in your browser from the statement already on screen rather than fetched again. The assistant still declines to say WHY a number is high - that inference it cannot make - but it will now show exactly WHAT the number is made of, which is the question people were actually asking. Nothing is taken on trust: the statement response carries a signed context binding its scope, outline, pinned batches, mapping-master version and user, so a question can be proven to be about the statement on screen and not merely about data you happen to be entitled to. Every refusal says which check failed. The transaction read keeps the drill's governed-read protections, auditing the exact predicate before it runs and failing closed. No figure the server read ever reaches the model - the explanation is composed on the server and the model only classifies the question. A statement built on a batch that has since been replaced still answers, and says so. The Ask page is untouched: it neither sends this context nor displays these explanations, and a grounded explanation is cleared the moment you generate a different statement, so an answer can never sit against figures it does not describe. SHIPPED UNEXERCISED: no host held both this code and real data, so the capability closes on hermetic proof under decision 0039, and its first run on the server is also its first proof (D-0055).

items.title: Ask filters by a comparison between measures
items.story: As a finance reader asking Ask about budget versus actual, I want 'which lines are over budget' and 'which GL codes spent more than 5 lakh' answered with only the matching lines, so that a verified answer never silently drops the condition I asked for.
acceptance_criteria: Selection gains an additive optional measureFilters list (measure vs measure or vs a fixed-scale decimal value, gt/gte/lt/lte, AND, order-preserving); filters is unchanged; saved queries, pins, the persisted turn, the conversation answer snapshot and Swagger accept it; shipped selection leaves pass unmodified.

Validation refuses with typed reasons a non-money operand, an operand outside the domain or the user's permissions, a self-comparison, a duplicate entry or a value outside ^-?\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$; % measures are not comparable; every check that reads measureIds reads the union with the operand measures.

The SQL builder compiles each measure filter to HAVING over the verified expressions in both the governed-financial query and the statement projection, and the statement projection now applies dimension filters as WHERE predicates; leaves assert the emitted SQL and the golden statement proofs stay unchanged.

Operand measures missing from measureIds are appended by the server in first-appearance order before validation and appear in the returned selection and chips; the first measure and the row ordering are unchanged.
Totals cover every matching group via a derived table without the inner LIMIT; a fixture with more matches than the page proves it.
The SQL validator accepts HAVING and the derived table while its object allowlist, blocked-column, no-star and bounded-LIMIT checks still fire; an empty result is a successful empty answer.

The selector tool schema enumerates only comparable measure ids in measureFilters; the system prompt maps over/under budget, over 100% and lakh/crore onto the shape; the parser refuses malformed entries; leaves assert schema, prompt and parser against recorded provider outputs.

Chips, saved-selection labels and the provenance readback render the comparison in words with registered labels and Indian digit grouping; appliedMeasureFilters is returned and snapshotted; selection identity includes the filter.

viewInReport is unavailable with the stated reason when a measure filter is present, and report grounding carries the question's measureFilters through; a leaf proves a grounded over-budget question never returns the unfiltered report.

Functional check live against Bedrock and the July warehouse: the three demo phrasings return only the matching lines with the Actual > Budget chip, and the DUB answer matches the statement rows whose % is above 100 or reads over-budget.
items.outcome: Ask now answers comparison questions such as list items where Actual is more than Budget, or GL codes above 5 lakh, by filtering in the database at GL-code and statement-line grain, shows the comparison as a readout and chips, keeps it in saved and pinned reports, and passed a live check against Bedrock and the July warehouse.

items.title: Ask names each GL line and opens its transactions
items.outcome: Ask answers now name every GL line from its SAP account names and every statement line by number and name, and clicking a transaction-backed Actual opens the SAP lines behind it, adding up to the figure to the paisa; live on July 2026 all 21 over-budget GL codes were named, 50001201 opened to ₹83,98,339, and a DUB statement line opened the same lines as the statement screen.

items.title: Every Ask answer works across plants
items.outcome: Ask answers across every plant: a plant picker with All plants, plant filters and breakdowns, combined statements that add up each plant's own, Budget-not-loaded dashes, and plant-safe names, transactions and saved views; the live check answered all five success questions on every run

items.title: Actual-versus-Budget answers ask for the period and every answer shows its dates
Ask preserves complete questions and opens every live Actual transaction set
